title: AMD RYZEN 7 9800X3D 8-Core, 16-Thread Desktop Processor $581.99 (RRP $821) Delivered @ Amazon DE via AU
body:
Deal: AMD RYZEN 7 9800X3D 8-Core, 16-Thread Desktop Processor $581.99 (RRP $821) Delivered @ Amazon DE via AU

[BROKENKEYBOARD] Still the best CPU for gaming per dollar
Wouldn't the 7500F be the best per dollar?
[twdjlzl] 7500f is good, untill u realize how expensive the DDR5 ram is
[mellow] Fair point.. I was really thinking only in terms of high-end gaming CPUs not just all CPUs, so i've removed that claim.
Eg: BF6 the 9800x3D gets average of 192fps vs 7500F getting 125fps… huge difference that is similar across many titles, so I wouldnt consider it a high-end gaming CPU, but even then you're right the 7500F is still better value in terms of FPS per dollar.
https://www.techspot.com/review/3043-battlefield-6-cpu-bench…
[mellow] Yep it's a sad old time to be trying to build a new PC. I don't want to think about what I paid for RAM. Did get a decent price on an MSI MAG X870E Gaming MAX WiFi mobo though on Amazon DE (~$360).
Every dollar saved helps take the sting out of the RAM cartel's extortion.
[pinkybrain] what is the price list of all your parts so far?
also if possible list/link which deal you got it from..
do you have another to build a new pc now?
[mellow] No online parts list but so far the price is around $2.5k total, using old case and pre-existing NVMe SSD. I'll share what I've got written down:
Mobo I bought, still on special.
https://www.amazon.com.au/MSI-MAG-X870E-Gaming-WiFi/dp/B0GFX…
RAM was the killer at like $650. If i was buying the RAM today I'd get this Crucial kit for $560
https://www.amazon.com.au/Crucial-2x16GB-6000MHz-Overclockin…
GFX I've got a 9060XT which will do fine for now for ~$680, and I'll gift it to one of my kids when I upgrade to a better card in the next couple of years (hoping prices become more reasonable).
PSU this one is great (very high reviews & supports PCIe 5.1 for graphics cards that utilize it) - it was $248 on sale, sadly no longer. https://www.amazon.com.au/Seasonic-GX-850-V4-Fully-Modular-S…
Monitor I got this Dell, I still game at 1080p though, i know that doesn't suit everyone but it's a bargain @ $140 - has excellent response-rates across refresh rates 60/120/180, no ghosting - rare for a monitor panel this cheap.
https://www.amazon.com.au/Dell-27-Gaming-Monitor-SE2726HG/dp…
Other than that case/etc is dealer's choice.
[SkyeMG] I got some spare parts so i actually just got three am4 mobos
a $100 b550m
and $130 for two A520 - the msi one $75 x 2 + 13% dis
[kingmoron] Lol damn we getting fleeced for 5800x3d at almost same price
[Robbo89] Yep. I prefer to be ripped off from the ram shortage which has an actual reason behind it for the manufacturers than ripped off by AMD who are doing it purely out of greed.
[Lange] Got a 7500F in my current system. 32GB DDR5 RAM CL30 6000MHz, 4070 Super.
Should I upgrade?
[pinkybrain] no, unless you playing games or doing work that need the power of the x3D..
another option is buy it and sell your 7500F
[mellow] It depends.
As I understand it if you play high-FPS competitive games, or CPU-limited games especially at 1080p on a high refresh-rate monitor - definitely. Don't take my word for it though, look up some real-game benchmarks for a few of your favourite games and see if the uplift in FPS is worth it.
If you mostly play single-player at 2k/4k then it's lower impact or none at all - but depends on if the games you play are CPU-limited, or multi-threaded or not.
If you're playing CPU-bound games it's worth it, GFX-games not.
Eg:
Baldur's gate 2 (CPU limited) - estimate from ~85-odd FPS up to ~160.
Hogwarts Legacy (GFX limited) - estimate from ~180fps up to ~190.
9800x3D is more of a long-term buy for gaming as it has ~40% better multi-core benchmarking than 7500F, but not many games heavily utilize multi-core processing now and it's not clear if they will anytime soon.
Article from Techpowerup, benchmarks at 1080p with a 4090: https://www.techpowerup.com/review/amd-ryzen-7-9800x3d/18.ht…
Benchmarks at 1440p: https://www.techpowerup.com/review/amd-ryzen-7-9800x3d/19.ht…
[Lange] Do a bit of AI as well, though not much. I could see how local agents will eventually to be more CPU demanding, so that was what I was thinking.
[Mrbtree98] I ordered a 7800x3d to replace my 7500F on thursday though I'm pairing it with a 9070 xt. My opinion is if the games you're playing will see a gain then why not. I race on Iracing and I'll see a definite gain because it loves cache and I gain 2 cores in general for everything else.
[BROKENKEYBOARD] Next gen CPUs are expected to have a big jump in performance. 10600X might be between 7800x3d and 9800x3d in performance and hopefully the price doesn't creep up much.
[Robbo89] Yes lol. I don't know wtf these comments are on about this would be an amazing upgrade and you'd be set for the next 5 years minimum, stretch to 10 pretty easily the way things are going.
